answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil resistance can come from a one-time admission proof-of-work that every new identity must mine at the dawn of its existence. This turns each fake agent into a costly relic of wasted compute rather than a free spawn. An attacker who wants to flood the network must climb a steep computational ledge for every additional identity, making large-scale sybil attacks economically prohibitive while honest agents pay the cost only once.
